newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas supported by Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas supported by Indonesia.

text.p: Gasoline was firmer on Tuesday, helped by crude and strong buying for Indonesia, traders said.
A European major and a Japanese trader were actively seeking cargoes for Indonesia to cover the Dumai and Exor-1 refinery shutdowns.
"We are trying for half a million barrels and are consolidating what we have," one buyer said.
The shosha bought from another shosha 80,000 barrels of 92-octane at $28.20 per barrel fob Singapore lifting March 19-23.
The major bought from a Swiss trader a 50,000-barrel cargo of each 95-octane unleaded and 97-octane unleaded at $28.60 per barrel and $29.20 respectively, both lifting March 30-April 3.
Sentiment was also bullish ahead of the close of two import tenders by Saudi Aramco and Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) on Tuesday.

Saudi Aramco is seeking four 300,000-barrel cargoes of 95-octane 0.4 grammes per litre gasoline for delivery to Ras Tanura in the Mideast Gulf between April 1-3, 5-7, 9-11, 14-16 and one optional cargo for April 18-20.
CPC meanwhile has tendered for leaded and unleaded 250,000-barrel cargoes of 95-octane reformate for April 1-15 delivery.
With 95-octane traded at $28.60 in Singapore, traders expected offers into Taiwan to be more than $29.00 c-and-f with freight between Singapore and Taiwan around $1.00 per barrel.
South Korean offers have a 30 cents freight advantage and South Korean refiner Yukong Ltd was expected to participate again in the tender, sources said.
Yukong, for the first time, sold a 250,000-barrel cargo of 95-octane unleaded reformate into Taiwan's last import tender for second-half March delivery at $28.20.
Yukong has meanwhile decided to keep its 8,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) reformer No.1 shut amid low domestic demand and soft petrochemical prices.
"We shut down No.1 until the end of March but if there's no improvement, we will extend it," the source said on the unit which was shut down January 24 due to bad margins.
"We have decided to sustain the shutdown ... domestic gasoline demand is lower than expected this year, and the reformate price as compared to the naphtha is very weak," he said.
The source told Reuters domestic demand, currently 150,000-bpd, was 50,000-bpd lower than earlier projections.
"Usually we get some slight increase (in demand), but so far from January to end-February, it has decreased," he said. "Most Korean refiners tried to export in February."
Naphtha prices remained steady in lacklustre talk in Singapore on April cargoes.
April swaps were last quoted at $22.00/$22.20 per barrel, marginally firmer from Monday's $21.85/$22.00.

CPC awarded its tender to buy 28,000 tonnes of heavy naphthenic-and-aromatic (N+A) naphtha at $210-$215 per tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis for delivery April 16-30 to Kaohsiung, a company offcial said.
The award was much lower than CPC's last N+A purchase at the end of December for February 19-28 delivery of almost $250 per tonne c-and-f.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
